name: Saitada

attributes.attribute: a British goddess linked to the Tyne valley
believed to stand for grief or sorrow

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Saitada is a British goddess. She belonged to the valley of the Tyne in northern Britain. Monaghan records that she may have stood for grief and sorrow. We know her from a single Roman inscription. That one stone is all that remains of her name. No myth about her survives, and no full article about her appears in the great reference works. Her worship was local. It left a narrow mark on the record. Our knowledge of her rests on one dedication carved by one worshipper. She is a reminder that most Celtic deities are known by fragments. Those few words tell us she owned a shrine, or at least a votive, in the land by the river.

okr.objective: Document Saitada, the British goddess of grief.
key_results: Record Saitada as a Tyne-valley divinity.
Record the belief that she represented grief or sorrow.
